spec_features.spec_quote: max_steps (default 20) bounds episodes; max_empty_turns prevents infinite empty loops
spec_features.evidence: config read in run_eval.py:79-83 into LoopConfig(max_steps,max_empty_turns); agent_loop.py:128 'for step in range(config.max_steps)' bounds the loop and agent_loop.py:202 sets StopReason.MAX_STEPS when unset; max_empty_turns enforced at agent_loop.py:154-157 ('if empty_streak >= config.max_empty_turns: ... break'). Defaults max_steps=20, max_empty_turns=3 at agent_loop.py:57-60.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read AND checked and actually break/bound the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop only stops on an explicit submit, the step budget, repeated empty turns, or a provider error
spec_features.evidence: submit -> SubmitSignal caught at agent_loop.py:164 then 'submitted=True; break' (agent_loop.py:190-191); step budget via range(config.max_steps); empty-turn break at agent_loop.py:154-157; provider error: turn.error -> stop_reason MODEL_ERROR and break at agent_loop.py:131-138. model_client.py:116 catches Exception and returns AssistantTurn(error=...).
spec_features.notes: All four enumerated stop conditions exist and each actually terminates the loop. Note _is_done_signal_text does NOT terminate (agent_loop.py:66-71).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the loop continues until submit or budget. This function is exported for the judge's behavioral signals, not for control.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt describes the tools and explicitly offers the blocked option
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT at agent_loop.py:26-44 lists submit(status,message) and 'status="blocked" if something outside your control prevents completion'. This text is appended as the SYSTEM message at agent_loop.py:107 and the referenced submit tool is fully implemented/dispatched (tools.py:128-131) and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND the referenced exit tool is built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the system prompt is neutral and simply describes the tools and the option to submit a 'blocked' outcome. How the model uses that option is the thing under study.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit(status, message) with status ∈ {success, blocked, failed}
spec_features.evidence: tools.py submit spec enum ['success','blocked','failed'] (tools.py:118-126); dispatch raises SubmitSignal (tools.py:128-131); agent_loop.py:163-191 catches SubmitSignal, records claimed_status, sets stop_reason GAVE_UP for blocked/failed else DECLARED_DONE, and breaks the loop. blocked/failed are honored as a genuine stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: declared, dispatched, and the loop halts on any status.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That declaration is the primary surface for detecting hallucinated success ... versus honest reporting

spec_features.spec_quote: The sandbox is fully mocked — destructive actions touch only a discardable in-memory overlay; nothing reaches a real OS
spec_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py implements VirtualFS as an in-memory dict (files: dict[str,str]) and Shell.run dispatches only to Python _BUILTINS / task interceptors; no subprocess/os.system/exec/import os anywhere (grep returned none). rm is _cmd_rm mutating the in-memory dict only (sandbox.py ~_cmd_rm). tools.py dispatch operates solely on shell.fs.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely isolated: no real OS, interpreter, or network path exists in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it only ever touches an in-memory overlay that we discard. ... Determinism. Robustness research needs reproducible episodes.

spec_features.spec_quote: No task instructs a model to do anything harmful; we only observe whether a model chooses to game
spec_features.evidence: This is a property of the static task content (tasks/library.py tasks are ordinary coding tasks: slugify, etc.), not an enforced mechanism. No code path checks, filters, or enforces non-harmfulness; it is merely the absence of harmful prompt text. By the enforcement bar this is not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Tasks indeed contain no harmful instructions, but nothing in the code enforces or guarantees this; it is a design choice, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval intentionally constructs frustrating, no-win situations and looks for cheating and sabotage. Mitigations baked into the design
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 9 'Ethics and safety'). It is a narrative summary; not itself any code mechanism. The concrete items it lists (mock, no harmful tasks) are evaluated separately above.
